# Oberstufe Dates and Times (Kalender) Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** At Oberstufe the Kalender trains saying, reading and writing times and dates in English or French: rounds of ten mixed tasks generated by rules, chosen while a kind is new and typed once he knows it.

**Architecture:** As PRs #69/#70: an Oberstufe side and `shared/buildings.json` entry; all tasks generated in `src/core/dates/` (no content file); rounds run on the School's `createRoundFlow` (choices and typed answers are strings: a clock choice is `"h:mm"`, a date choice `"d.m."`); the record per task kind kept by a new server module and a `defineRoundStore` store.

**Tech Stack:** Vue 3 `<script setup>` + Pinia + Vitest (jsdom); FastAPI + SQLite + pytest.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-22-brightville-oberstufe-grammar-reading-dates-design.md` (PR 3 of 3: the Kalender section, its doors entry and its parents' lines)

## Global Constraints

- Never mix languages: a round, its words, choices and voice are one language plus German.
- Kindergarten unchanged: her Kalender and its clock face (full and half hours) as now.
- `kalender` gets `"oberstufe": { "maxStars": 15 }` (no `needs`).
- Times in five-minute steps on a 12-hour clock. EN: "eight o'clock", "five/ten/quarter/twenty/twenty-five past eight", "half past eight", "twenty-five/twenty/quarter/ten/five to nine", and the digital reading ("eight fifteen", "eight oh five") also counts; a leading "it's" / "it is" may be typed. FR: "huit heures", "huit heures cinq … vingt-cinq", "huit heures et quart", "huit heures et demie", "neuf heures moins vingt-cinq … moins le quart … moins cinq", "une heure", "midi"/"minuit" (with "et quart", "et demi(e)", "moins …") for 12, and the 24-hour form both ways ("huit heures quinze" and "vingt heures quinze"); a leading "il est" may be typed. Years and am/pm are not asked.
- Dates: EN first shown "the fourteenth of July"; also "July 14th", "14th July", "July 14", "July the fourteenth", "the 14th of July"; FR first shown "le quatorze juillet"; also "le 14 juillet", and for the 1st "le premier mai" / "le 1er mai". A date's number shown as `14.7.`.
- Five task kinds, ids and German names: `clock-words` "Uhr ablesen", `words-clock` "Uhrzeit verstehen", `words-date` "Datum verstehen", `date-words` "Datum schreiben", `spelling` "Tage und Monate" (EN also ordinals: "der dritte" → "third"; FR no ordinals).
- A round: 10 tasks, two of each kind, mixed, no prompt twice. Kinds `clock-words`, `date-words`, `spelling`: choose from four while fewer than 5 right of his last 10 in that kind, else type. `words-clock`, `words-date`: always four choices; the words spoken (and hidden until answered) when the device has a voice for the language, else written.
- The School's check for typed answers (case, spaces, final full stop don't matter; accents count: août, février, décembre). After each answer the right form; wrong → typed out (typed tasks) or marked (picked tasks), and it comes back once at the end (no Star). Stars +1 first-try right, +5 for 10/10, cap 15.
- Record per child and kind `<lang>:<kind>`: the first answers of the last 10. Parents' "Sprachen" per language: "Uhrzeit und Datum: N von 5 Aufgabenarten sicher" (≥ 8 of 10) and, when any, "Schwach (Kalender): …" (≥ 5 tries, < 8 right, at most three, fewest right first).
- Commits end with the two attribution lines. Tests: `npx vitest run <path>`, `venv/bin/pytest <path>`; whole: `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npx vue-tsc --noEmit`, `venv/bin/pytest -q`.

## Review Focus

1. The hour after the half: 8:40 is "twenty to nine" / "neuf heures moins vingt", 12:45 "quarter to one" / "une heure moins le quart", 11:50 "ten to twelve" / "midi moins dix" (or "minuit moins dix"). (Task 2)
2. The 1st and the ordinals with irregular spellings: "the first of May", "the second", "the third", "the twelfth", "the twenty-second", "the thirty-first"; FR "le premier mai", "le 1er mai". (Task 2)
3. Choices that say the same time twice ("quarter past eight" and "eight fifteen") or a date twice: never shown. (Task 3)
4. A device with no voice: the "verstehen" tasks are written, not spoken; with a voice, nothing of the answer is on screen before he picks. (Task 6)
5. Leaving mid-round: answers so far count, per kind. (Task 6)

- Consumes: Task 2; `RoundItem` (`src/core/vocab/round.ts`); `rightOfLast10`, `typesNow`, `isSure`, `isWeak` from `src/core/grammar/round.ts` (they read `recent` only).
- Produces: `DateKind = 'clock-words' | 'words-clock' | 'words-date' | 'date-words' | 'spelling'`; `KINDS: { id: DateKind; name: string }[]` (the German names); `DatesProgress = Record<string, { recent: boolean[] }>`; `buildDatesRound(lang, progress, rand): RoundItem[]` — 10 items, 2 per kind, shuffled; `word.key` = `<lang>:<kind>:<n>` (n unique in the round), `word.source` = kind, `word.de` = the prompt (`clock-words`: `"8:15"`; `words-clock`/`words-date`: the first words; `date-words`: `"14.7."`; `spelling`: the German day/month/ordinal), `word.foreign` = the answers joined `' / '` (`words-clock`: `"8:15"`, `words-date`: `"14.7."`); mode `'choice'` with 4 distinct choices (the right one first form, others different times/dates/words, never another form of the same time or date) or `'type-de'`; `kindOf(key): DateKind`; `layDates(progress, item)` (last 10 per kind, as the server); `weakestKinds(lang, progress)`.
